newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil leases production ship for China oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil leases production ship for China oilfield.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) and Chinese National Offshore Co (CNOOC) have jointly contracted with Lufeng Development Co to lease a production ship for the Lufeng 22-1 oilfield in the South China Sea, Statoil said on Thursday.
The contract, worth about 600 million crowns, runs for two years with options to extend.
The ship, with a production capacity of 60,000 barrels per day, is due for delivery in June 1997. Bergesen ASA with be responsible for the maritime operations of the vessel.
The vessel is the second of three sister ships under construction for Statoil in South Korea, Statoil said.
Lufeng 22-1 lies 250 km southwest of Hong Kong in a water depth of 330 metres. Recoverable reserves are estimated at 35 million barrels of oil.
Lufeng Development Co comprises Statoil, together with Norwegian companies Advanced Production Systems (APS) and Stolt Comex Seaway.
CNOOC has a 25 percent interest in the field and Statoil 75 percent. Statoil (Orient) Inc, based at Shekou in China, will operate the development.
